# the contributor audit: spectral reduction and finite two-corner area frontier


`candidate e32081eac0270dbc`
and Sections 1--3 of
`candidate 29c2230b74378948`
as first read. The subsequently appended incidence classification is not
included in this audit.

## Spectral objective: PASS

For positive three-edge data the largest eigenvalue is simple with a
strictly positive eigenvector. The absolute-value Rayleigh argument and
orthogonality of eigenvectors prove this without a spectral gap assumption.
The projective inverse-chord parameter makes all three edge entries affine,
with one positive and two negative nonzero derivatives. Its derivative
matrix is invertible because its determinant is the product of the three
edge derivatives divided by four. At a stationary parameter, the vector
D w is therefore nonzero and perpendicular to w. Substituting
w+epsilon c D w in the Rayleigh quotient gives exactly the stated positive
quadratic term, with a bounded cubic remainder, for both signs of epsilon.
Thus the strict stationary-coordinate assertion is stronger than convexity
alone and is fully justified.

The fixed-area feasible radii are closed, bounded above, and bounded away
from zero by the displayed diagonal and adjacent product constraints.
The objective is continuous, so its maximum is attained. Increasing a
radius up to a core bound increases the entries of the symmetric Z-matrix;
the absolute-value quadratic comparison preserves PSD. Decreasing a
radius in a positive-definite principal complement is feasible for a small
change. Homogeneity supplies both derivative signs unless all vanish;
the just-proved stationary gain handles the latter case.

I checked the listed four two-core patterns and the single singular block
patterns of sizes one through four against their radius changes. Each
claimed exchange keeps its separating core products fixed, improves the
singular block entrywise, and changes only a positive-definite complement
elsewhere. The displayed objective variations have the asserted sign.
Consequently a maximum has at least two cores and two singular blocks.
The previously audited sparse-slack reconstruction gives at most four
vertices while retaining the maximizing six sector areas and endpoints.

The final statement correctly retains both triangles and quadrilaterals
without a cap restriction. Only the stated cap ceiling invokes the separate
incidence theorem to exclude triangular cubic failures. The reduction does
not preserve neighboring mixed fibers and does not itself prove the
quadrilateral inequality.

## Finite reciprocal-area frontier: PASS

For a triangle kernel normalized to (alpha,beta), alpha+beta=1, the
two-node block is lambda [[beta^2,-alpha beta],[-alpha beta,alpha^2]].
Adding a corner loss l times the all-ones matrix has determinant lambda l.
Its first and second inverse diagonal entries are respectively
alpha^2/l+1/lambda and beta^2/l+1/lambda. The formula is exact, including
the stated finite-area normalization l=1/(2X)-1/(2X_T).

Testing the full changed matrix on an unchanged corner's positive kernel
proves that either adjacent positive gain is impossible. With exactly two
positive losses, only their joining double edge can grow. On those four
nodes the matrix is blockdiag(C_i,C_j)-g aa^T. Conjugation by the positive
square root proves PSD if and only if g a^T blockdiag(C_i,C_j)^(-1) a<=1,
which is precisely the printed frontier. The other corner block is
decoupled. Along with the explicitly retained area/core bounds, the exact
sector realization theorem therefore makes this condition sufficient as
well as necessary.

At finite positive equality the four-node block has rank three; the
unchanged two-node block has rank one. The reconstructed polygon therefore
has exactly four vertices. This rank count does not require strictness of
the changed unique-sector core inequalities. No cubic sign has been
deduced from feasibility alone.

These are ordinary planar results. Full OC remains unproved.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
